c.python:
class Solution:
    def distinctDifferenceArray(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        cnt = Counter()
        suf = [0] * (n + 1)
        d = 0
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            cnt[nums[i]] += 1
            if cnt[nums[i]] == 1: d += 1
            suf[i] = d  # distinct in nums[i..]
        cnt = Counter()
        ans, d = [], 0
        for i in range(n):
            cnt[nums[i]] += 1
            if cnt[nums[i]] == 1: d += 1
            ans.append(d - suf[i + 1])
        return ans

a.t: O(n) — two linear passes with hash maps
a.sp: O(n) for counters and suffix array

w: Lead with brute force to establish correctness, then present the two-pass solution as the scalable answer. Pitfall: suffix array indexing — suf[i+1] must exclude nums[i] itself; empty suffix contributes 0. Follow-up: generalize to arbitrary split points (prefix sums of distinctness don't compose, so offline/Mo's algorithm ideas come up).
